title: Paired high-versus-low demand signed-overshoot specificity on SOTS-Outdoor
rationale: The completed signed measurement established materially prevalent overshoot in high-demand regions, but low-demand overshoot was descriptively at least as large. This direct within-source comparison freezes the existing region and overshoot definitions, averages hazy variants within each clear-source group, and estimates the paired high-minus-low difference with a fixed group bootstrap. It performs no training, threshold selection or protected-data access.

orthogonal_changes.reason: The parent prevalence estimand asked whether overshoot occurs within high-demand regions; it did not compare the same source groups against low-demand regions and therefore could not establish demand specificity.

scientific_contract.question: Across 492 independent SOTS-Outdoor clear-source groups, is the materially overshot-tile fraction at least 5 percentage points higher in the highest-demand 20 percent of tiles than in the lowest-demand 20 percent within the same source groups?

intervention.reference: lowest-demand 20 percent of paired input-error tiles within the same hazy variant and clear-source group
intervention.matched_budget: all 500 hazy variants nested within exactly 492 clear-source groups; one fixed official checkpoint; zero training or model selection
fixed_factors: all 492 GT images and all 500 paired hazy images are used at original resolution with no scientific-data resizing
official Dehazing.OTS build_net('base') is strictly loaded from checkpoint state_dict['model']; input is reflect-padded to a multiple of 32 and model(input)[2] is cropped and clipped to [0,1]
non-overlapping 32 by 32 tiles are formed after reflect-padding image arrays only to a multiple of 32
high-demand and low-demand tiles are respectively the exact top and bottom 20 percent of tile mean RGB input-to-GT squared error with stable row-major tie breaking
for each tile, signed projection coefficient alpha is dot(prediction-input, GT-input) divided by squared norm(GT-input) plus 1e-8
signed projected overshoot magnitude is max(alpha minus 1, zero) times the RMS norm of GT-input in the tile
a tile is materially overshot only when alpha is at least 1.05 and projected overshoot magnitude is at least 1/255
for each hazy variant the contrast is high-demand materially overshot-tile fraction minus low-demand materially overshot-tile fraction
multiple hazy variants are averaged within their clear-source group before inference; every clear-source group has equal weight
the primary estimate is the arithmetic mean of 492 source-group contrasts
uncertainty is a two-sided percentile bootstrap with seed 3407 and 10000 resamples of the 492 source groups
direction counts use an absolute zero tolerance of 1e-12 and two-sided Wilson 95 percent intervals
missing or failed source groups remain visible and prevent a definitive PASS or FAIL

primary_estimand.metric: mean within-source-group difference in materially overshot-tile fraction, high-demand minus low-demand
primary_estimand.aggregation: equal-weight source-group mean with fixed-seed 10000-resample paired percentile bootstrap 95 percent interval

controls: strict identity-bound official OTS checkpoint and official production graph
full-image input-to-output MSE improvement as a global-competence prerequisite
paired high and low regions are selected within the same hazy variant from model-output-independent input-to-GT error
the parent signed-overshoot closeout identity and complete SOTS aggregate identity must match
a protected-data-free reference case independently checks variant averaging, contrast direction and source-group equal weighting
all hazy variants remain nested within their original clear-source group

uncertainty.method: two-sided percentile paired bootstrap over 492 independent clear-source groups with seed 3407 and 10000 resamples; variants, tiles and pixels remain nested

gates.estimand: checkpoint, model sources, parent signed-overshoot closeout, complete SOTS pairing and aggregate dataset identity match
independent source groups with every paired variant and finite inference
Wilson lower 95 percent bound for source groups whose variant-mean full-image output MSE is below input MSE
paired-bootstrap interval for the source-group mean high-minus-low materially overshot-tile fraction
paired-bootstrap upper 95 percent bound for the same high-minus-low contrast

scientific_contract.competing_explanation: Even a positive paired difference would remain a descriptive association with input-error rank rather than proof that haze demand causally creates over-dehazing. A nonpositive difference would support a broader local overshoot tendency, but paired RGB GT can still contain alignment, color or compression differences, output clipping can hide excursions, and SOTS clear-source overlap with OTS training is not excluded.
disabled_actions: training, fine-tuning, module insertion, loss selection, threshold tuning or candidate selection during this route
changing the parent tile, region, alpha or absolute materiality definitions after observing the paired result
treating tiles, pixels or hazy variants as independent samples
interpreting a positive association as a causal haze mechanism or automatic module requirement
treating SOTS outcomes as strict unseen-source generalization because clear-source overlap with OTS training is not excluded
relabeling SOTS as confirmation or sealed-final evidence after this development-screening use
Haze4K outcome, NH-HAZE, confirmation, canary or locked-test access
changing image membership, preprocessing, grouping, metrics, margins, bootstrap seed, resample count, controls or terminal rules after outcomes

precision_contract.rationale: Using the conservative bound SD<=1 for a contrast in [-1,1], 492 groups give a normal-approximation 95 percent half-width no larger than 1.96/sqrt(492)=0.0884, below the frozen 0.09 feasibility target; the full available SOTS population is used.

capability.production_path_statement: The exact official Dehazing.OTS build_net('base') graph strictly loads the official OTS checkpoint and executes the production reflect-pad-to-32, model(input)[2], crop, clip, paired high-versus-low signed-overshoot contrast and result-finalizer path on one synthetic CUDA tensor without scientific data.

precision.estimand: mean source-group high-minus-low materially overshot-tile fraction
precision.source_reference: The contrast is bounded in [-1,1]; ceil((1.96/0.09)^2)=475 and all 492 source groups are used.
